comparison: Both evaluate DEG analysis and pathway enrichment (C27-C30). OpenEval finds the analysis SUPPORTED with appropriate statistical thresholds, while peer review rates it UNCERTAIN due to lack of functional validation of BBB permeability changes despite methodologically sound transcriptional profiling.

Both assess astrocyte DEG analysis (C31-C33). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED but notes interpretive nature of BBB connection claims. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, emphasizing lack of functional assays to validate BBB permeability or cytokine release despite documented transcriptional changes.

Both evaluate microglial DEG analysis (C34-C36). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with comprehensive enrichment analyses but notes speculative BBB interpretation. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, highlighting absence of functional validation despite methodologically sound transcriptional profiling.

Both acknowledge the limitation regarding missing pericytes and neurons (C120). Both rate this SUPPORTED as an appropriately recognized limitation. Peer review connects this to broader concerns about lacking details on BBB opening magnitude and spatial distribution.

Both evaluate cell type identification (C4-C5, C22-C26). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with appropriate marker gene expression and annotation methods, noting pericyte/neuron absence as limitation. Peer review also rates SUPPORTED, describing it as 'valuable finding' with 'solid and validated' methodology.

Both assess prior EA effects on BBB (C2, C9-C12). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to apparent contradiction between EA-induced opening vs. protective effects and lack of direct BBB permeability measurement. Peer review also rates UNCERTAIN, noting foundational importance but lacking 'key details regarding magnitude, duration, and spatial distribution of BBB opening.'

Both evaluate experimental methodology (C3, C13, C20-C21). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with clearly described design, though notes limited sample size and permissive QC thresholds. Peer review rates SUPPORTED, stating 'data were collected and analyzed using solid and validated methodology' without questioning technical approach.

OpenEval evaluates endothelial subset heterogeneity (C37-C42) as SUPPORTED with appropriate pathway enrichment but unclear biological significance. Peer R7 covers broader endothelial analysis (C37-C63) rated UNCERTAIN, noting comprehensive transcriptional mapping but inadequately explained rationale and lack of functional validation.

OpenEval evaluates EC_Cluster0 'basic response' interpretation (C43-C50) as SUPPORTED with appropriate pathway enrichment and citations. Peer R7 includes these claims in broader endothelial analysis rated UNCERTAIN due to inadequate experimental rationale and lack of functional validation despite molecular insights.

OpenEval evaluates comparative cluster analysis (C51-C53) as SUPPORTED with clear presentation and appropriate enrichment. Peer R7 includes these in comprehensive endothelial analysis rated UNCERTAIN, emphasizing lack of functional validation for BBB opening relevance.

OpenEval evaluates EC_Cluster4 BBB-relevant genes (C54-C59) as SUPPORTED, noting downregulation of barrier genes but interpretive complexity. Peer R7 includes these in broader endothelial analysis rated UNCERTAIN due to lack of experimental confirmation of functional relevance to BBB opening.

OpenEval evaluates EC_Cluster5 analysis (C60-C63) as SUPPORTED with clear functional implications but speculative protein synthesis interpretation. Peer R7 includes these claims in comprehensive endothelial analysis rated UNCERTAIN, noting molecular insights lack functional confirmation.

OpenEval evaluates microglial subset analysis (C64-C69) as SUPPORTED with comprehensive documentation supporting 'crucial priming cells' speculation. Peer R8 covers broader microglial analysis (C64-C86) rated UNCERTAIN, acknowledging methodological soundness but emphasizing lack of functional validation and speculative nature of priming cell claim.

OpenEval evaluates upregulated microglial genes (C70-C78) as SUPPORTED with well-supported enrichment analyses and identification of BBB-relevant genes. Peer R8 includes these in broader microglial analysis rated UNCERTAIN due to lack of functional assays to validate findings despite methodological soundness.

OpenEval evaluates downregulated microglial genes (C79-C86) as SUPPORTED with comprehensive analysis and BBB-relevant pathways. Peer R8 includes these claims in broader microglial analysis rated UNCERTAIN, noting methodological soundness but absence of functional validation.

Both evaluate cell-cell communication analysis using CellPhoneDB (C87-C92). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with appropriate methodology but notes computational predictions require validation and potential rat-to-human conversion inaccuracies. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, emphasizing lack of functional assays to validate predicted interactions or consequences for BBB permeability.

OpenEval evaluates detailed ligand-receptor pairs (C93-C96) as SUPPORTED with biologically relevant signaling changes but inferred directionality. Peer R9 includes these in broader communication analysis rated UNCERTAIN due to computational derivation and lack of functional validation.

OpenEval evaluates comprehensive cell-endothelial interactions (C97-C102) as SUPPORTED, noting systems-level view but unclear biological significance. Peer R9 includes these in communication analysis rated UNCERTAIN, emphasizing computational nature and absence of functional validation.

OpenEval evaluates discussion synthesis and interpretations (C108-C117) as UNCERTAIN, noting speculative nature of many claims including microglial priming role and inferential connections between gene expression and BBB function. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these discussion claims.

OpenEval evaluates literature-based background claims (C103-C106, C118-C119) as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate citations of established knowledge though relevance to current findings not always clear. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.
